before: RICE_bamian_repair_shahr_e_zohak_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historical Context:#! Shahr-e Zohak is one of the most impressive fortifications ever built in Afghanistan; one scholar even called it the "Afghan Krak des Chevaliers." It was occupied by successive groups, such as the Hephthalites, Ghaznavids, Ghurids, and Timurids. Zohak is an evil figure in Persian mythology, and though it is uncertain why the fortress is named after him, he is said to be the ancestor of the nearby Ghurids. A legend has it that the fortress city was destroyed by Genghis Khan, and all its inhabitants massacred as revenge for his grandson's death when it was besieged."

before:
yorkshire.0106.desc:0 "I am reflecting over the life and times of Alcuin, that famous scholar and monk from York and who became an important intellectual of Charlemagne’s court. He trained many important thinkers of his era, and I feel a little sense of pride at the thought that I rule territories not too far from where he was born and grew up in. Two of his famous sayings, I recall, include:

"Remember to care for the soul more than the body, since the former remains, the latter perishes."

"And do not listen to those who keep saying, 'The voice of the people is the voice of God', because the tumult of the crowd is always close to madness.""

before: rice_vajrayana_canon_doctrine_desc:0 "The Tantric Canon is the collection of Buddhist texts accepted by the so-called esoteric schools of Buddhism, such as Tibetan Vajrayana and sects influenced by them. These canons include Mahayana texts, as well as texts from early schools of Buddhism that are not part of or were discarded from the Pali Canon."

before:
north_atlantic.0208.info:0 "
#emphasis Historical Context:#! Dairy products have been consumed in Northern and Western Europe for centuries, and #italic skyr#! is the name of the Icelandic variant of yogurt. Interestingly, in the Icelandic sagas, serving items like milk, cheese, or yogurt to guests was considered improper, particularly if other food could be provided. Being immersed in milk products could be considered especially humiliating.

In one episode of the #italic Egil's Saga#!, for instance, the protagonist Egil and his companions visit a man named Armod, who only serves them #italic skyr#!. Egil takes this as a great insult, and, in revenge, vomits the yogurt all over Armod, who in turn vomits back at Egil. When Armod's men ask why Egil did such a thing, he says, "Don’t blame me for following the master of the house’s example. He’s spewing his guts out just as much as I am.""

before:
north_atlantic.0273.desc:0 "Though I am young, I have already learned much from the schools here in the British Isles. I have greater ambitions, however, when it comes to scholarly matters; my knowledge of mathematics, various languages, and especially astronomy will carry me far, as I seek to better understand the great universe which [ROOT.Char.GetFaith.HighGodName] created.

The skies are marked with numberless sparks, each a fire, and I know these stars well. I have seen in these stars that it is perhaps my time to travel far from here, and learn more and more about this world. Maybe, one day, I can even become one of the greatest astrologers in the world.

#weak "Every astrologer is worthy of praise and honor, since by such a doctrine as astrology, he knows many secrets of [ROOT.Char.GetFaith.HighGodName], and things which few know."#!"

The skies are marked with numberless sparks, each a fire, and I know these stars well. I have seen in these stars that it is perhaps my time to travel far from here, and learn more and more about this world. Maybe, one day, I can even become one of the greatest astrologers in the world.

#weak "Every astrologer is worthy of praise and honor, since by such a doctrine as astrology, he knows many secrets of [ROOT.Char.GetFaith.HighGodName], and things which few know."#!"

before: RICE_lesbos_fortify_aegean_decision_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historical Context:#! Since ancient times, the [GetGeographicalRegion('RICE_aegean_region').GetNameNoTooltip] has attracted frequent piracy, maritime raids, and naval warfare due to its strategic geographical location. For instance, a young Julius Caesar was captured by pirates in the Aegean Sea; he "jokingly" promised them they would be crucified after his ransom was paid, and he did, in fact, later capture and kill these pirates. Over the centuries, the peoples of the region would develop different ways to protect themselves from such attacks."

before:
lesbos.0051.desc:0 "We have tolerated the presence of pirates in my territories for far too long. Our "agreements" with them have not been working in our favor, and even though many are also respectable merchants, can we really trust them when they are no less greedier than the average charlatan and bandit?

I have thus sent out an order to immediately renege on any of our agreements with pirate groups in the [GetGeographicalRegion('RICE_mediterranean_region').GetName]. They will no longer be afforded legal protections nor the ability to set up their base of operations in my territories by working with us, because they no longer work #italic for#! us.

I have ordered my troops to make sure these pirates comply with our commands. We can only hope they leave peaceably...."

before: RICE_reinforce_relations_silk_road_communities_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historical Context:#! The lands along the so-called "Silk Roads" have been home to a blend of many ethnicities, religions, and cultures, then and now. In various urban centers, diverse communities of different origins often played major roles in local affairs despite their "foreign" origin. before: RICE_tarim_basin_compile_the_turkic_dictionary_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historical Context:#! Diwan Lughat al-Turk, or "Compendium of the Languages of the Turks," is the magnum opus of Mahmud al-Kashgari, a Karakhanid scholar who was possibly distantly related to the ruling Karakhanid clan. Written in 1072-1074 CE, it was intended for use by the Caliphs of Baghdad who were under Seljuk domination. The book was not only a mere dictionary, as it also included a map of the world from Japan to Egypt, various notes on history and geography, and examples of old Turkic poetry. As the first Turkic dictionary, it is a valuable historical resource."

As the first Turkic dictionary, it is a valuable historical resource."

before: tarim_basin.0240.desc:0 "Many learned [ROOT.Char.GetFaith.GetReligion.GetAdjective] scholars say that China once consisted of three divisions: Tabgach in the south; Khitay in the north; and Barkhan or Kashgar in the west, in the [GetGeographicalRegion('world_steppe_tarim').GetName], where I now hold significant amounts of territory. I will become the first in my family to have honorary titles recognizing my dominion over this region which used to be dominated by the Chinese Empire, such as #italic Malik al-Mashriq wa al-Sin#! before:
harran.0062.desc:0 "I sit in the darkness of my library, sipping mint tea as my acquaintance enters the room. He is a scholar from the House of Wisdom who I worked with back when I lived in Baghdad, and he gives a smile as he joins me. I offer him some tea, and we chat pleasantly about various topics to catch up.

Eventually, our conversation drifts towards the topic of religion. "I heard something interesting about your grandfather [hilal_al_sabi.GetFullName] the other day," my friend tells me.

This again? I shift uncomfortably, but don't say anything yet, and continue sipping my tea."

before:
harran.0063.desc:0 "“You have said for many years that your grandfather converted to Islam thanks to a dream, a sure sign from Allah himself.” My friend smiles. "One of my mentors, an older gentleman, who was acquainted with your grandfather, said he never heard of such a thing, but admits perhaps his memory is not as it used to be thanks to old age. I don’t doubt you, but it does make me wonder if your grandfather was telling the truth - no offense to him.” 

I stroke my chin and gaze at my friend quietly. Many question my grandfather's story. I know this.

I ponder how to respond."

We sip tea for a few more moments, savoring the taste, before I continue: "Now, not to change the subject, but have you read the new treatise written by….""

before:
harran.0065.desc:0 "“But what?” he says.

I frown.

"I don't mean to imply he was secretly an apostate, but…." I consider my words carefully. "I always felt he had sympathy for his birth religion. I could tell by the way he talked fondly of our ancestors."

"The scholarly achievements of Harran's pagans are nothing to laugh at! Your forebear, [thabit_ibn_qurra.GetFullName], was a rare scholar of his age." My friend nods. "But if your grandfather's heart is genuine, thanks to that dream, then that is all that matters. Sure, you still have a few wayward relatives who still believe your old gods, and I know you were never the most pious man, but at least you are a believer, too, right?""

before:
khwarezm.0014.desc:0 "The citadel of Al-Fir in [kath.GetNameNoTier] has stood proudly for many years. This beautiful and mighty fortress can be seen for miles and miles, and served as a symbol of the local rulers' might and prestige. Alas, it also happens to be located next to the Amu Darya or Oxus River, nicknamed the "Mad River" due to its tendency to change course or overflood erratically.

Over the years, the citadel has managed to withstand assault after assault by the waters of the Oxus, but its defenses have gradually worn out. Though the main structure of the fortress is still standing, it is partly ruined, and local authorities have deemed it no longer safe to use on a large scale, and the administration has relocated to other structures in town.

Still, at least the citadel remains standing. Even if it is no longer in frequent use, it will surely continue to inspire and embolden the inhabitants nearby."

before:
bao.0001.desc:0 "My soldiers bring forth two young black-costumed men whom they arrested outside my residence.

"This low-born rabble was found sleeping in a dried ditch, my [ROOT.Char.GetLadyLord]," one of my soldiers says when asked who they are. "They say they are church musicians, but they were acting suspiciously, and it is clear they are highway robbers who are using your property without permission."

Another soldier interjects, "While I do agree they are acting suspiciously, we shouldn't be too hasty to make any judgment.

The first soldier ignores the other's comment, and says, "They are highwaymen, whether you like it or not, so I suggest we give them a swift exemplary punishment for trespassing.""

before: bao.0001.info:0 "#emphasis Historical Context:#! Up until the mid XXth century, costumes were the most reliable way to tell the social status of a stranger; in Brittany, black costumes were un-embroided costumes for the poorest of the poor. The "Sonerien Du" or "Black Musicians" were traveling singers and musicians paid mostly in food and drink, who went from church to church, mass to mass, and wedding to wedding to do their trade. They had the reputation of playing "hep diskrog" or "restlessly" and according to local superstition, a Breton wedding could only end when the musician was too drunk to play. They often were seen as troublemakers by the Gendarmes and the upper stratas of Breton society.\n The actual "Sonerien Du" legend which is the reference for the event is the legend of the Bro Vigouden (Barony of Kemper) where two black-coated musicians were unjustly punished around 1790 in Pont-'n-Abad (Pont-l'-Abbé in French) and sentenced to death for sleeping dead drunk in the roadside, either because they were mistaken for highway robbers or as the result of the corruption of the local aristocracy. Their bodies were exposed on spikes for everyone to see. Because this event coincided with (unverified) plague outbreaks, people held them as martyrs, and would touch the bodies, believing it would grant plague immunity."

before:
VIETkemet.0003.desc:0 "After changing into humbler clothes, my companions and I now look like ordinary if well-off travelers. The villagers are hospitable to us "travelers" and happily provide us accommodations. It is auspicious that we have come at this time, they say.

Standing in the village square, in the midst of a throng of men, women, and children, I watch as the feast to Osiris proceeds. Some villagers take pigs with them and bring the animals before an altar of the god. They slit the throats of the unfortunate beasts, an offering no doubt to Osiris, before giving the carcasses to swineherds who take the bodies away.

Afterwards, a great cheer erupts, as everyone begins to fill the village square to celebrate. I enjoy drinking good beer and dancing with the other villagers. Soon enough, one villager, playing the flutes, happily skips around playing a lively tune, and we all follow after him while singing praises to Osiris."

"I am bringing the gods incense and natron.
I want to expel the bad smell from your mouth.
Therefore I come in order to expel the evil in your hearts.
With this I remove the Evil, Isfet, which clings to you.
With this I bring you Good.
I present Justice, Maat, to you......""

before:
normandy.0091.info:0 "
#emphasis Historical Context:#! Whatever the truth of William and Matilda's relationship, there are legends of questionable veracity about how it began. Supposedly, Matilda rejected William's offer of marriage, as she saw herself, daughter of the Count Baldwin of Flanders, as too high-born for a "bastard."

The Duke, in his rage, went all the way to her home in Flanders. In some versions of the legend, he found her going to church and, in broad daylight, dragged her off her horse by her braids and pushed her into the mud before riding off. In other variations, he went to her father's manor, and dragged her by her braids or hit her in full view of everyone, Baldwin included. Afterwards, Matilda bizarrely only wanted to marry William.

In reality, the marriage was probably arranged under more mundane political circumstances. The Counts of Flanders were powerful, and a potential threat to Normandy's east. By marrying into their family, William not only avoided conflict with them, but also gained a valuable ally."

before:
game_concept_mahavihara_desc:0 "The Mahavihara, alongside the [abhayagiri|E] and [jetavana|E], are one of the three major [RICE_sri_lanka_monasteries|E] in the [RICE_sri_lanka_struggle|E], or its Buddhist community. In-game, the Mahavihara are represented by an orange icon: @RICE_mahavihara_icon!.

You can raise or lower the [RICE_sri_lanka_prominence|E] of the Mahavihara through different [decisions|E], [activities|E], and so on, especially if you have the [GetTrait('RICE_mahavihara_trait').GetName( GetNullCharacter )] [trait|E], which can be gained by taking the [decision|E] to $RICE_sri_lanka_choose_monastic_sect$. Keep this in mind if you wish to end the [struggle|E] in [RICE_sri_lanka_short|E].

Historically, the Mahavihara were the more 'traditionalist' monastery or sect of ancient and medieval Sri Lankan Buddhism. They were typically skeptical or dismissive of what they saw as heterodox ideas from India. According to traditional chronicles, they were the ones who "won" out in the end against the other monasteries."

before: RICE_sri_lanka_worship_local_deities_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historical Context:#! For centuries, the people of Sri Lanka have worshipped a variety of shared deities, regardless of whether they are Buddhist or Hindu, or Sinhala, Tamil, or Vedda. Many of these deities were syncretized forms of Hindu, Buddhist, and indigenous religious figures, known by different names from different communities and often worshipped in a manner distinct from mainland India. For the island's Buddhists, while the Buddha is considered superior to these "lesser" deities, the latter are often invoked for more worldly concerns."

before:

We pray to remind ourselves about the importance of the Three Jewels – the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha – as we make offerings where the Dharmadhatu lays. I reflect on the Dharmadhatu while doing so.

The text itself expounds on the #italic Trikaya#! or "three bodies" teaching on the nature of reality and Buddhahood, found in the [GetDoctrineType('rice_mahayana_canon_doctrine').GetBaseName]. Some detractors criticize the Dharmadhatu’s teachings as unorthodox, even heretical, but others believe its spiritual ideas can help and guide all, and so it is worthy of veneration."

before: activity_RICE_yazidi_tawus_geran_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historical Context:#! Tawûs Gêran, the "Touring of Tawûs," is a Yazidi ceremony that involves the parading of a #italic sanjak#!, a standard of Melek Taus (the Peacock Angel). #italic Qewals#!, who are hereditary performers of Yazidi religious hymns, would thus bring with them the #italic sanjak#! as they travel to different Yazidi villages, as long as it is a time of peace adn when they are certain the roads are safe. It is an opportunity for Yazidis to learn about their religious beliefs and show their religious devotion. before: RICE_granada_alhambra_decision_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historical Context:#! The Alhambra (from Arabic #italic Al-Hamra#!, meaning "the Red One") was a palace and fortress complex of the Nasrid dynasty of Granada, and the epitome of medieval Moorish architecture. As a self-contained city, it had its own amenities likes bathhouses and mosques, and was continually expanded by the Nasrids from the 13th to 15th centuries. before:
granada.0014.desc:0 "I was sleeping at my manor in [granada.GetNameNoTier] when my guards woke me late at night - chaos has erupted in the city's streets!

Apparently, a false rumor had spread earlier today that the Jewish official [yusuf.GetFullName] and other Jews had defected to an enemy ruler, opened the city gates, and killed me. Thanks to recent, rising anti-Jewish sentiment, a mob quickly formed to "protect" the city. Obviously, I’m alive and [granada.GetNameNoTierNoTooltip] is safe.

Before I know it, [yusuf.GetFirstName] arrives in a panic, begging for help. Moments later, the mob storms my palace, screaming how they will kill the "traitor" [yusuf.GetFirstName] before going for his fellow Jews next. I rush to meet the mob to reassure them that I am fine and demand they stand down, but they pay no heed.

The mob is now moving fast towards [yusuf.GetFirstName], and I and my guards have little time to react."

before: granada.0032.desc:0 ""Oh, [abu_jafar.GetFirstName]! Even now I still dream of you, and your embrace, and your lips upon mine. Did I take you for granted? Did I not appreciate you enough while you were alive?"\n\nOthers may question why I often wear the clothes of a mourning widow, even now, when [abu_jafar.GetFirstNameNoTooltip] and I were never officially married. Truly, though, [abu_jafar.GetSheHe] was a remarkable [abu_jafar.GetWomanMan] and poet, and even now I am inspired to compose some poetry about [abu_jafar.GetHerHim]. before: granada.0033.desc:0 ""We used to exchange so many poems with each other. Sometimes [abu_jafar.GetFirstName] would initiate our exchange, and sometimes I would. Every time I write a poem, now, I think of those happy, young, carefree days...."\n\nIt is hard for me to compose poetry, still. It is not hard in a technical sense, but in an emotional sense. Every word of poetry I utter is a painful reminder of [abu_jafar.GetFirstNameNoTooltip]. I need to take a break from poetry... find other things to do... at least for a short while."

before: RICE_sicily_second_pavia_decision_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historical Context:#! Pavia was the capital of the Lombard Kingdom that dominated Italy from the 6th to 8th centuries, until its defeat by the Carolingian Franks. Lombard successor states emerged in southern Italy, and Benevento, a major center of Lombard power there, was even known as a "second Pavia" due to its prosperity and prominence. Ironically, these same Lombard polities were often dominated by the Franks to the north. The Lombards in the south would remain a distinct identity up until the era of Norman Sicily in the 12th and 13th centuries."
after: RICE_sicily_second_pavia_decision_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historical Context:#! Ironically, these same Lombard polities were often dominated by the Franks to the north. The Lombards in the south would remain a distinct identity up until the era of Norman Sicily in the 12th and 13th centuries."

before: RICE_sicily_byzantine_syracuse_decision_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historical Context:#! Syracuse was one of the great cities of the ancient Mediterranean; Cicero, for instance, described it as "the greatest Greek city and the most beautiful of them all." It retained its importance during the early Byzantine period, particularly after the empire's loss of its African territories; it even briefly served as the capital of the empire from 663-669 CE. With the Muslim conquest of Sicily, including the fall of Syracuse in 878, the island's center moved to Palermo, and while Syracuse still remained a major city on the island, it never regained its former preeminent status."

before: RICE_sicily_catania_elephant_decision_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historical Context:#! #italic U Liotru#! is a famous elephant statue in the city of Catania. The name is a corruption of Heliodorus, a legendary 8th century necromancer and sorcerer who either brought the statue to life, or transformed into it himself, before he was defeated by Saint Leo of Catania. Though the legend is of dubious historicity, the city has been associated with the statue for centuries; the Arabs called Catania the "city of the Elephant," and the geographer al-Idrisi, who worked at the court of King Roger II of Sicily, believed the statue was made by the Carthaginians or Romans and that the Catanese considered the statue to be magical and able to protect them from Mount Etna's eruptions. In 1239, the statue was chosen to be the city's symbol. After an earthquake, it was repurposed into a fountain in 1737."

In 1239, the statue was chosen to be the city's symbol. After an earthquake, it was repurposed into a fountain in 1737."

before: sicily.0001.desc:0 ""Sicily was the first of our provinces; Sicily first taught our ancestors how glorious it could be to rule other peoples." So said the great Roman Cicero, long before Rome declined in the West.\n\nSicily, crucible of the Mediterranean, is now a wild frontier where three worlds meet: Islam, Byzantium, and the Latin West. Many covet Sicily and its abundance, but would-be conquerors and settlers often find behind this paradise is a liminal land where the boundaries between culture, faith, and loyalty can be very blurry."

before: sarvastivada_desc:0 ""Sarvastivada" means the "theory that all exists," based on the argument that all dharmas, or phenomena, exist in the past, present, and future. This school has a strong Abhidharma (or scholastic) tradition, with seven unique Abhidharma works, and over the course of its history has exerted a significant influence on the development of Indian Buddhist philosophy and theology."

before: breton.0028.desc:0 "I am almost finished with the Tro Breizh, for I now arrive in Vannes, the seventh and last stop on this pilgrimage. It is, despite being a very ancient settlement - dating to before the Roman Emperors, learned men tell me - a very joyous and exciting place as well. I found, for example, much amusement in the comically puffy, ugly granite statues the locals dub "Vannes and his Wife." Some of the locals also explained the lore of the ancient large stones that dot the area.\n\nBut this is a time for religion, not mirth. I reflect on the Saint of Vannes, Saint Patern. They say this Saint was a contemporary of the mighty King Arthur, the great Briton hero; he tamed the king's avarice and humbled the monarch according to the legends. At any rate, I too, must practice the virtues. This is why I went on this pilgrimage after all."

before: RICE_bozo_mud_masons_decision_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historical Context:#! Mudbricks have been a conspicuous part of buildings in West Africa for centuries, with the Mosque of Djenne as perhaps the most famous example of this style of architecture. Mud masons are respected throughout the region for their practical, spiritual, and sorcerous knowledge, as construction requires not only creating the building, but also the use of spells and incantations to bless the site and exorcise evil spirits. For example, many mud masons in the city of Jenne are of the Bozo ethnicity, and are well-versed in Islamic Quranic verses and what they refer to as #italic bai bibi#!, or "African secrets," the details of which they seldom disclose to outsiders."

before: RICE_bozo_move_jenne_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historical Context:#! Jenne-Jeno ("Old Jenne"), the original site of Jenne, was a major urban center in present-day Mali but was abandoned sometime in the medieval period. According to legend, this move happened when the Soninke migrated to the region; they tried to establish a town near the original site settled by the Bozo, but were met with various natural disasters. They were only able to found the city after an oracle told them to sacrifice a virgin girl by burying her alive in the city walls. The tomb of this girl, known as Tapama Djenepo (i.e. "Tapama, the Martyr of Djenne"), still stands in modern Jenne."

before:
socotra.0009.desc:0 "We have tolerated the presence of pirates in my territories for far too long. Our "agreements" with them have not been working in our favor, and even though many are also respectable merchants, can we really trust them when they are no less greedier than the average charlatan and bandit?

I have thus sent out an order to immediately renege on any of our agreements with pirate groups in the [GetGeographicalRegion('RICE_indian_ocean_region').GetName]. They will no longer be afforded legal protections nor the ability to set up their base of operations in my territories by working with us, because they no longer work #italic for#! us.

I have ordered my troops to make sure these pirates comply with our commands. We can only hope they leave peaceably...."

before: RICE_khuzestan_khuzi_status_decision_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historical Context:#! Early medieval Islamic sources mention the existence of a so-called Khuzi people, who spoke a language that modern scholars theorize to be a late remnant of ancient Elamite. Although Khuzi was spoken by local nobility, this may have been because they learned it from their servants (such as wet-nurses, bathroom attendants, and so on). The Khuzis were otherwise treated as low status; for example, #italic "yā Xuz̄ı!"#!, meaning "Hey, you Khuzi!" was reported by the 10th century Arab geographer Al-Maqdisi as a common, slang term of insult in the region. Because of this, the Khuzi identity and language likely faded away as the Khuzis assimilated into Arab or Iranian populations."

The Khuzis were otherwise treated as low status; for example, #italic \"yā Xuz̄ı!\"#!, meaning \"Hey, you Khuzi!\" was reported by the 10th century Arab geographer Al-Maqdisi as a common, slang term of insult in the region. Because of this, the Khuzi identity and language likely faded away as the Khuzis assimilated into Arab or Iranian populations."

before: RICE_pamir_restore_hephthalite_empire_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historical Context:#! The Hephthalites, sometimes called the White Huns, were a major wave of "Hunnic" tribal invaders into Persia and India in the 4th and 5th centuries. Their relationship with "Hunnic" groups like the Kidarites and Xionites, the ethnic differences between these groups (if any), and where they came from, is still debated in academic circles - there are too many theories to be listed here, but suffice to say, Iranian and Turkic influence in their origins is likely, and it is possible that the Pamirs are their homeland. A Persian and Turkic alliance defeated them in c. 560 CE and the Hephthalite Empire split into many petty chiefdoms. Prominent among these Hephthalite rump states were the Turkshahis and their cousins, the Zunbils."

before:
lesbos.0051.desc:0 "We have tolerated the presence of pirates in my territories for far too long. Our "agreements" with them have not been working in our favor, and even though many are also respectable merchants, can we really trust them when they are no less greedier than the average charlatan and bandit?

I have thus sent out an order to immediately renege on any of our agreements with pirate groups in the [GetGeographicalRegion('RICE_mediterranean_region').GetName]. They will no longer be afforded legal protections nor the ability to set up their base of operations in my territories by working with us, because they no longer work #italic for#! us.

I have ordered my troops to make sure these pirates comply with our commands. We can only hope they leave peaceably...."

before: yorkshire.0055.desc:0 "Es ist Morgen, und heute ist der große Tag - die Stierhatz von Stamford steht vor der Tür! Die Glocken der örtlichen [ROOT.Char.GetFaith.HouseOfWorship] werden geläutet, um allen mitzuteilen, dass das Stiertreiben bald beginnen wird. Der Ausrufer der Stadt verkündet dann allen Bürgern, dass sie ihre Läden und Tore schließen sollen. Als sich alle versammeln, riecht es stark nach "Stierdreck" - einer Mischung aus Erde und Stierexkrementen, mit denen sich viele als Glücksbringer beschmiert haben. Sobald alles geregelt ist, wird der Stier freigelassen, und das Getümmel beginnt: Männer, Frauen und Kinder jagen dem Stier hinterher!"

before:
yorkshire.0104.desc:0 "Ein Spiel namens "Knurr and Spell" wird in Yorkshire immer beliebter, vor allem bei den einfachen Leuten in Tavernen und Pubs. Sogar Adlige beginnen sich daran zu erfreuen.

Bei diesem Spiel versuchen die Spieler, einen Ball (den #italic Knurr#!) mit einem Stock (dem #italic Spell#!) so weit wie möglich zu schlagen. Nach mehreren Runden wird der Spieler zum Sieger erklärt, der den Ball im Durchschnitt am weitesten schlägt.

Auf jeden Fall wurde ich eingeladen, dieses Spiel mit einigen Bekannten zu spielen. Das könnte eine gute Gelegenheit sein, mein Können in dieser Art von Wettbewerb unter Beweis zu stellen."

before: yorkshire.0106.desc:0 "Ich reflektiere über das Leben und die Zeit von Alkuin, dem berühmten Gelehrten und Mönch aus York, der ein bedeutender Intellektueller am Hof von Karl dem Großen wurde. Er bildete viele bedeutende Denker seiner Zeit aus, und ich empfinde ein wenig Stolz bei dem Gedanken, dass ich Gebiete beherrsche, die nicht allzu weit von dem Ort entfernt sind, an dem er geboren wurde und aufgewachsen ist. Zwei seiner berühmten Sprüche, an die ich mich erinnere, lauten:\n\n"Kümmere dich mehr um die Seele als um den Körper, denn ersterer bleibt, letzterer vergeht." "Und höre nicht auf die, die immer wieder sagen: 'Die Stimme des Volkes ist die Stimme Gottes', denn der Tumult der Menge ist immer dem Wahnsinn nahe.""

before: yorkshire.0111.desc:0 "Ich fahre durch [west_riding_county.GetNameNoTier], insbesondere durch ein Gebiet, das als #bold Ilkley-Moor#! bekannt ist. Dort gibt es eine große Felsformation, die von den Einheimischen "Kuh und Kalb" genannt wird, weil sie den beiden ähnelt. Der örtlichen Legende zufolge waren die beiden Felsen einst eine Einheit, bis der Riese Rombauld (der einst in Yorkshire lebte) vor dem Zorn seines Feindes - lustigerweise seiner eigenen Frau - floh und bei der Verfolgung versehentlich auf den Felsen stampfte, wodurch dieser in zwei Teile gespalten wurde.\n\nWie auch immer, es ist ein schöner Anblick, und die Felsen heben sich elegant von den übrigen Gräsern und dem Himmel ab."

before: red_sea.0037.desc:0 "Ich habe einen wichtigen muslimischen Adeligen zu Gast, der gerade seine Pilgerreise nach Mekka beendet hat und nun auf dem Heimweg ist. Als ich ihn bitte, mir zu erzählen, wie sein Abenteuer verlaufen ist, berichtet er mir, dass der furchterregendste Teil der Reise die Überquerung des Roten Meeres mit einer Fähre war:\n\n"Ich war noch nie auf dem Meer gewesen", erklärt er. "Ich musste mich die ganze Zeit an meiner Sklavin festhalten, damit ich mich nicht übergeben musste. Sie war in einem Küstenland geboren und an das Leben auf einem Boot gewöhnt, und sie lachte mich wegen meiner Schwäche aus - ich hätte das streitlustige Mädchen auf der Stelle auspeitschen können, wenn ich sie nicht so gern gehabt hätte... oder vielleicht war mir einfach zu mulmig, um zu reagieren...".”"

Sie war in einem Küstenland geboren und an das Leben auf einem Boot gewöhnt, und sie lachte mich wegen meiner Schwäche aus - ich hätte das streitlustige Mädchen auf der Stelle auspeitschen können, wenn ich sie nicht so gern gehabt hätte... oder vielleicht war mir einfach zu mulmig, um zu reagieren...\".”"

before: RICE_sicily_second_pavia_decision_desc:0 "After the fall of the Kingdom of the Lombards, and the loss of their glorious capital, Pavia, the Lombards' heirs have wandered and survived in southern Italy. after: RICE_sicily_second_pavia_decision_desc:0 "After the fall of the Kingdom of the Lombards, and the loss of their glorious capital, Pavia, the Lombards' heirs have wandered and survived in southern Italy. Establishing [GetPlayer.GetCapitalLocation.GetTitle.GetNameNoTier] as a \"second Pavia\" will be an important step in reviving the fortunes of the [GetPlayer.GetCulture.GetName] people."

before: RICE_sicily_second_pavia_decision_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historical Context:#! Pavia was the capital of the Lombard Kingdom that dominated Italy from the 6th to 8th centuries, until its defeat by the Carolingian Franks. Lombard successor states emerged in southern Italy, and Benevento, a major center of Lombard power there, was even known as a "second Pavia" due to its prosperity and prominence. Ironically, these same Lombard polities were often dominated by the Franks to the north. The Lombards in the south would remain a distinct identity up until the era of Norman Sicily in the 12th and 13th centuries."
after: RICE_sicily_second_pavia_decision_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historical Context:#! Pavia was the capital of the Lombard Kingdom that dominated Italy from the 6th to 8th centuries, until its defeat by the Carolingian Franks. Lombard successor states emerged in southern Italy, and Benevento, a major center of Lombard power there, was even known as a \"second Pavia\" due to its prosperity and prominence. Ironically, these same Lombard polities were often dominated by the Franks to the north. The Lombards in the south would remain a distinct identity up until the era of Norman Sicily in the 12th and 13th centuries."

before: RICE_sicily_byzantine_syracuse_decision_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historical Context:#! Syracuse was one of the great cities of the ancient Mediterranean; Cicero, for instance, described it as "the greatest Greek city and the most beautiful of them all." It retained its importance during the early Byzantine period, particularly after the empire's loss of its African territories; it even briefly served as the capital of the empire from 663-669 CE. With the Muslim conquest of Sicily, including the fall of Syracuse in 878, the island's center moved to Palermo, and while Syracuse still remained a major city on the island, it never regained its former preeminent status."
after: RICE_sicily_byzantine_syracuse_decision_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historical Context:#! With the Muslim conquest of Sicily, including the fall of Syracuse in 878, the island's center moved to Palermo, and while Syracuse still remained a major city on the island, it never regained its former preeminent status."

before: RICE_sicily_catania_elephant_decision_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historical Context:#! #italic U Liotru#! is a famous elephant statue in the city of Catania. The name is a corruption of Heliodorus, a legendary 8th century necromancer and sorcerer who either brought the statue to life, or transformed into it himself, before he was defeated by Saint Leo of Catania. Though the legend is of dubious historicity, the city has been associated with the statue for centuries; the Arabs called Catania the "city of the Elephant," and the geographer al-Idrisi, who worked at the court of King Roger II of Sicily, believed the statue was made by the Carthaginians or Romans and that the Catanese considered the statue to be magical and able to protect them from Mount Etna's eruptions. In 1239, the statue was chosen to be the city's symbol. After an earthquake, it was repurposed into a fountain in 1737."

before: sicily.0001.desc:0 ""Sicily was the first of our provinces; Sicily first taught our ancestors how glorious it could be to rule other peoples." So said the great Roman Cicero, long before Rome declined in the West.\n\nSicily, crucible of the Mediterranean, is now a wild frontier where three worlds meet: Islam, Byzantium, and the Latin West. Many covet Sicily and its abundance, but would-be conquerors and settlers often find behind this paradise is a liminal land where the boundaries between culture, faith, and loyalty can be very blurry."

before:
VIETkemet.0003.desc:0 "Nachdem wir uns bescheidenere Kleidung angezogen haben, sehen meine Begleiter und ich wie gewöhnliche, wenn auch wohlhabende Reisende aus. Die Dorfbewohner sind gastfreundlich zu uns "Reisenden" und stellen uns bereitwillig eine Unterkunft zur Verfügung. Es sei ein Glücksfall, dass wir zu dieser Zeit gekommen sind, sagen sie.

Auf dem Dorfplatz stehend, inmitten einer Schar von Männern, Frauen und Kindern, beobachte ich den Ablauf des Festes des Osiris. Einige Dorfbewohner nehmen Schweine mit und bringen die Tiere vor einen Altar des Gottes. Sie schlitzen den unglückseligen Tieren die Kehle auf, zweifellos ein Opfer für Osiris, bevor sie die Kadaver den Schweinehirten geben, die sie abtransportieren.

Danach bricht großer Jubel aus, als alle beginnen, den Dorfplatz zum Feiern zu füllen. Ich genieße ein gutes Bier und tanze mit den anderen Dorfbewohnern. Bald darauf hüpft ein Flötenspieler fröhlich umher und spielt eine lebhafte Melodie, und wir alle folgen ihm, während wir ein Loblied auf Osiris singen."

before:
VIETkemet.0011.desc:0 "Der Hexenpriester versteht meine Sorgen und kennt die richtige Beschwörungsformel für meine Situation. So beginnt er in meiner Gegenwart zu singen:
"Ich bringe den Göttern Weihrauch und Natron.
Ich will den üblen Geruch aus eurem Munde vertreiben.
Daher komme ich, um das Böse in euren Herzen zu vertreiben.
Damit entferne ich das Böse, Isfet, das euch anhaftet.
Damit bringe ich euch das Gute.
Ich überreiche euch die Gerechtigkeit, Maat......""

before: VIETkemet.0020.desc:0 "Ich besuche einen nahegelegenen Tempel, als ich einen Mann in einer Ecke sitzen sehe, der mit kleinen Instrumenten und Waagen etwas abmisst, was Weihrauch zu sein scheint. Als ich ihn frage, was er da treibe, antwortet er mir mit Nachdruck: "Es ist meine Pflicht, die monatlichen Weihrauchrationen für die Schreine und Altäre dieses Tempels und für die Priester, die dort arbeiten, abzuwiegen. Meine Arbeit ehrt Dedwen, den Gott und Herrn des Weihrauchs, und ist unerlässlich. Bitte, lasst mich mich konzentrieren.""

before: rice_vajrayana_canon_doctrine_desc:0 "The Tantric Canon is the collection of Buddhist texts accepted by the so-called esoteric schools of Buddhism, such as Tibetan Vajrayana and sects influenced by them. The Tibetan Canon for example consists of the Kangyur ("Translation of the Word") and Tengyur ("Translation of Treatises"). These canons include Mahayana texts, as well as texts from early schools of Buddhism that are not part of or were discarded from the Pali Canon."
after: rice_vajrayana_canon_doctrine_desc:0 "The Tantric Canon is the collection of Buddhist texts accepted by the so-called esoteric schools of Buddhism, such as Tibetan Vajrayana and sects influenced by them. The Tibetan Canon for example consists of the Kangyur (\"Translation of the Word\") and Tengyur (\"Translation of Treatises\"). These canons include Mahayana texts, as well as texts from early schools of Buddhism that are not part of or were discarded from the Pali Canon."

before:
harran.0047.desc:0 "Doch nun bin ich zu Hause, als Anführer ganz Harrans! Das ist eine große Ehre, aber auch eine wenig beneidenswerte Aufgabe. Einige von uns sagen, dass in diesem Zeitalter der neuen Religionen unsere Aussichten, als eigenständige Gemeinschaft zu überleben, gering sind. Ich widerspreche dem nicht. Die Zeit läuft gegen uns. Es gibt nur wenige, die die alten Bräuche von Völkern wie den Ägyptern und Griechen praktizieren.

Als die Sonne unterzugehen beginnt, gehe ich weiter die Straße hinunter und komme schließlich zu dem großen Tempel in Harran. Auf dessen Portal sind die Worte von Platon, unseres verehrten Vorvaters, eingemeißelt: "Derjenige, der sein eigenes Wesen kennt, findet zu den Göttern".
\Ich lese das Zitat mehrmals, bevor ich in den immer dunkler werdenden Abendhimmel blicke. Ich betrachte die Sterne und tue so, als könnte ich irgendwie unser Schicksal lesen, bevor ich den Heimweg antrete."

before: harran.0060.desc.caliph:0 "\n\nNachdem wir ein angenehmes intellektuelles Gespräch geführt haben, bringe ich mein Angebot erneut zur Sprache. " Habt Ihr über mein Angebot nachgedacht, Euch zum Vorsteher von Harran zu ernennen? Immerhin ist es der Heimatort Eurer Familie. Seid Ihr immer noch interessiert?""

before: harran.0060.desc.non_caliph:0 "\n\nWährend wir ein angenehmes intellektuelles Gespräch führen, erwähne ich ein Gerücht, das ich kürzlich gehört habe. "Stimmt es, dass [Kalif_dude.GetTitledFirstName] Euch angeboten hat, Euch zum Anführer von Harran zu ernennen? Ich kann mir vorstellen, dass das eine große Ehre wäre, da Harran der Heimatort Ihrer Familie ist.""

before: harran.0060.b:0 ""Ich werde nach Harran gehen, ja", antwortet er. "Das ist mein Schicksal.""

before:
harran.0061.desc:0 "Es ist viele Jahre her, seit ich durch die Straßen von [harran_county.GetNameNoTier] gegangen bin. Einst fruchtbares Ackerland wird zu Staub; Menschen wandeln sich, wachsen, sterben; und das Leben geht weiter, unbeständig wie immer. Aber die Sterne am Himmel? Sie bleiben, wie sie immer waren und wie sie immer sein werden. Diejenigen, die in den Sternen lesen, wissen, dass das Schicksal einen eigenen Willen haben kann.

Es ist eine seltsame Fügung des Schicksals, dass [caliph_dude.GetTitledFirstName] mich zum neuen Anführer von Harran auserkoren hat. Die Stadt war im Niedergang begriffen, was vielleicht mit dem Niedergang ihrer alten heidnischen Gemeinschaft und ihrer Gelehrten zusammenhing.

 Ich komme an den Ruinen der alten Neoplatonischen Akademie und dann an den Ruinen des Tempels des Mondes vorbei. Ich lasse mich auf die Knie fallen, durchstöbere ein wenig Schutt und finde die Überreste des Tempelportals. Ich kann immer noch die in das Holz geritzten Worte Platons erkennen: "Wer sein eigenes Wesen kennt, findet zum Göttlichen."
\Ich lese das Zitat mehrmals, bevor ich in den immer dunkler werdenden Abendhimmel aufschaue. Ich betrachte die Sterne und tue so, als könnte ich irgendwie unser Schicksal lesen, bevor ich den Weg nach Hause finde."

before:
harran.0062.desc:0 "Ich sitze in der Dunkelheit meiner Bibliothek und schlürfe Minztee, als mein Bekannter den Raum betritt. Er ist ein Gelehrter aus dem Haus der Weisheit, mit dem ich zusammengearbeitet habe, als ich noch in Bagdad lebte, und er lächelt, während er sich zu mir setzt. Ich biete ihm Tee an, und wir unterhalten uns angeregt über verschiedene Themen, um uns auszutauschen.

Schließlich schweift unser Gespräch auf das Thema Religion ab. "Ich habe neulich etwas Interessantes über deinen Großvater [hilal_al_sabi.GetFullName] gehört", sagt mein Freund zu mir.

Das schon wieder? Ich bewege mich unbehaglich, sage aber noch nichts und nippe weiter an meinem Tee."

before:
harran.0063.desc:0 ""Du sagst seit vielen Jahren, dass dein Großvater dank eines Traums, eines sicheren Zeichens von Allah selbst, zum Islam übergetreten ist." Mein Freund lächelt. "Einer meiner Mentoren, ein älterer Mann, der Deinen Großvater kannte, sagte, er habe so etwas noch nie gehört, aber er gibt zu, dass sein Gedächtnis aufgrund des hohen Alters vielleicht nicht mehr so gut ist wie früher. Ich zweifle nicht an Dir, aber ich frage mich, ob Dein Großvater die Wahrheit gesagt hat - ohne ihm zu nahe treten zu wollen." 

 Ich streiche mir über das Kinn und schaue meinen Freund ruhig an. Viele stellen die Geschichte meines Großvaters in Frage. Ich weiß das.

 Ich überlege, wie ich antworten soll."

before: harran.0064.desc:0 ""Vielleicht hat sich mein Mentor aufgrund des hohen Alters falsch erinnert", zuckt mein Freund mit den Schultern. "Ich will natürlich nicht Deinen eigenen Glauben in Frage stellen. Ich dachte nur, es sei etwas Interessantes. Wie dem auch sei, ich bringe Dich wahrscheinlich in Verlegenheit, also entschuldige ich mich dafür."\n\n"Natürlich", sage ich höflich. Wir nippen noch ein paar Augenblicke am Tee, genießen den Geschmack, bevor ich fortfahre: "Nun, ich möchte nicht das Thema wechseln, aber hast du die neue Abhandlung gelesen, die von....""

before:
harran.0065.desc:0 ""Aber was?", fragt er.

Ich runzle die Stirn.

"Ich will nicht andeuten, dass er insgeheim ein Abtrünniger war, aber...." Ich überlege meine Worte sorgfältig. "Ich hatte immer das Gefühl, dass er Sympathien für seine Geburtsreligion hatte. Das merkte ich daran, wie herzlich er von unseren Vorfahren sprach."

"Die gelehrten Errungenschaften der Heiden von Harran sind nicht zum Lachen! Dein Vorfahre, [thabit_ibn_qurra.GetFullName], war ein außergewöhnlicher Gelehrter seiner Zeit." Mein Freund nickt. "Aber wenn das Herz deines Großvaters dank dieses Traums aufrichtig ist, dann ist das alles, was zählt. Sicher, du hast immer noch ein paar abtrünnige Verwandte, die an deine alten Götter glauben, und ich weiß, dass du nie der frommste Mann warst, aber wenigstens bist du auch gläubig, oder?""

before: KITAB_AJA_IB_AL_HIND_GLOSS:0 "The #bold Kitāb ʿajāʾib al-Hind#!, or #italic "The Book of the Marvels of India"#!, is a tenth century collection of the adventurous tales of merchants, sailors, and travelers written by Buzurg ibn Shahriyār, an Arab sea captain. It was dedicated to an Ikhishidid governor of Egypt, Abu al-Misk Kafur (905 - 968 CE), who was originally an African slave serving the Ikhshidids but rose through the ranks to become #italic de facto#! ruler of Egypt as vizier before becoming sole ruler in 966."

before: RICE_greenland_sunset_invasion_legend_chapter_motivation_struggle:0 "When the peoples native to the western Atlantic first encountered the peoples of Eurasia, sometimes their interactions were peaceful, with increased trade and diplomacy. before:
north_atlantic.0208.info:0 "
#emphasis Historical Context:#! Dairy products have been consumed in Northern and Western Europe for centuries, and #italic skyr#! is the name of the Icelandic variant of yogurt. Interestingly, in the Icelandic sagas, serving items like milk, cheese, or yogurt to guests was considered improper, particularly if other food could be provided. Being immersed in milk products could be considered especially humiliating.

In one episode of the #italic Egil's Saga#!, for instance, the protagonist Egil and his companions visit a man named Armod, who only serves them #italic skyr#!. Egil takes this as a great insult, and, in revenge, vomits the yogurt all over Armod, who in turn vomits back at Egil. When Armod's men ask why Egil did such a thing, he says, "Don’t blame me for following the master of the house’s example. He’s spewing his guts out just as much as I am.""

north_atlantic.0273.desc:0 "Though I am young, I have already learned much from the schools here in the British Isles. I have greater ambitions, however, when it comes to scholarly matters; my knowledge of mathematics, various languages, and especially astronomy will carry me far, as I seek to better understand the great universe which [ROOT.Char.GetFaith.HighGodName] created.

The skies are marked with numberless sparks, each a fire, and I know these stars well. I have seen in these stars that it is perhaps my time to travel far from here, and learn more and more about this world. Maybe, one day, I can even become one of the greatest astrologers in the world.

before: RICE_bozo_mud_masons_decision_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historical Context:#! Mudbricks have been a conspicuous part of buildings in West Africa for centuries, with the Mosque of Djenne as perhaps the most famous example of this style of architecture. Mud masons are respected throughout the region for their practical, spiritual, and sorcerous knowledge, as construction requires not only creating the building, but also the use of spells and incantations to bless the site and exorcise evil spirits. For example, many mud masons in the city of Jenne are of the Bozo ethnicity, and are well-versed in Islamic Quranic verses and what they refer to as #italic bai bibi#!, or "African secrets," the details of which they seldom disclose to outsiders."

before: RICE_bozo_move_jenne_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historical Context:#! Jenne-Jeno ("Old Jenne"), the original site of Jenne, was a major urban center in present-day Mali but was abandoned sometime in the medieval period. According to legend, this move happened when the Soninke migrated to the region; they tried to establish a town near the original site settled by the Bozo, but were met with various natural disasters. They were only able to found the city after an oracle told them to sacrifice a virgin girl by burying her alive in the city walls. The tomb of this girl, known as Tapama Djenepo (i.e. "Tapama, the Martyr of Djenne"), still stands in modern Jenne."

before: RICE_khuzestan_khuzi_status_decision_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historical Context:#! Early medieval Islamic sources mention the existence of a so-called Khuzi people, who spoke a language that modern scholars theorize to be a late remnant of ancient Elamite. Although Khuzi was spoken by local nobility, this may have been because they learned it from their servants (such as wet-nurses, bathroom attendants, and so on). The Khuzis were otherwise treated as low status; for example, #italic "yā Xuz̄ı!"#!, meaning "Hey, you Khuzi!" was reported by the 10th century Arab geographer Al-Maqdisi as a common, slang term of insult in the region. Because of this, the Khuzi identity and language likely faded away as the Khuzis assimilated into Arab or Iranian populations."

The Khuzis were otherwise treated as low status; for example, #italic \"yā Xuz̄ı!\"#!, meaning \"Hey, you Khuzi!\" was reported by the 10th century Arab geographer Al-Maqdisi as a common, slang term of insult in the region. Because of this, the Khuzi identity and language likely faded away as the Khuzis assimilated into Arab or Iranian populations."

before: RICE_yazd_city_of_windcatchers_desc:0 "Due to Yazd‘s location along the edge of the #italic Dasht-e Kavir#! desert, windcatchers - tall towers that trap and channel air to provide natural ventilation and cooling - are ubiquitous in the city, giving rise to its nickname, "City of Windcatchers." before: RICE_pamir_restore_hephthalite_empire_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historical Context:#! The Hephthalites, sometimes called the White Huns, were a major wave of "Hunnic" tribal invaders into Persia and India in the 4th and 5th centuries. Their relationship with "Hunnic" groups like the Kidarites and Xionites, the ethnic differences between these groups (if any), and where they came from, is still debated in academic circles - there are too many theories to be listed here, but suffice to say, Iranian and Turkic influence in their origins is likely, and it is possible that the Pamirs are their homeland. A Persian and Turkic alliance defeated them in c. 560 CE and the Hephthalite Empire split into many petty chiefdoms. Prominent among these Hephthalite rump states were the Turkshahis and their cousins, the Zunbils."

before: chios.0077.desc:0 "Ich habe gehört, dass die Bewohner von Psara, einer einsamen Insel westlich von Chios, ein äußerst raues und hartes Leben führen und dass dies schon seit vielen Generationen, wenn nicht Jahrhunderten so ist - selbst die alten Griechen sprachen von der Armut der Insel in legendären Termini. So gab es in alten Zeiten die Redewendung "Psara feiert Dionysos, den Gott des Weines", um die Armut zu bezeichnen, denn man glaubte, die Bewohner der Insel seien so arm, dass sie sich nicht einmal ein wenig Wein bei wichtigen Festen leisten könnten. Offensichtlich hat sich seither auf der Insel nicht viel verändert."

before: chios.0100.desc:0 "Das Zusammenkommen mit den Mönchen verlief zufriedenstellend. Sie baten um einen angemessenen Betrag, um ihnen beim Bau eines kleinen Klosters auf Patmos bei der Höhle der Apokalypse zu helfen, wo Johannes von Patmos - der oft mit Johannes dem Apostel und Johannes dem Evangelisten in Verbindung gebracht wird - das Buch der Offenbarung geschrieben haben soll.\n\nSchließlich stimmte ich zu, dass es nur angemessen ist, eine so bedeutende Persönlichkeit zu verehren, wenn auch auf einer einsamen, kleinen Insel wie Patmos. before: RICE_tarim_basin_compile_the_turkic_dictionary_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historical Context:#! Diwan Lughat al-Turk, or "Compendium of the Languages of the Turks," is the magnum opus of Mahmud al-Kashgari, a Karakhanid scholar who was possibly distantly related to the ruling Karakhanid clan. Written in 1072-1074 CE, it was intended for use by the Caliphs of Baghdad who were under Seljuk domination. The book was not only a mere dictionary, as it also included a map of the world from Japan to Egypt, various notes on history and geography, and examples of old Turkic poetry. As the first Turkic dictionary, it is a valuable historical resource."

before:
khwarezm.0014.desc:0 "The citadel of Al-Fir in [kath.GetNameNoTier] has stood proudly for many years. This beautiful and mighty fortress can be seen for miles and miles, and served as a symbol of the local rulers' might and prestige. Alas, it also happens to be located next to the Amu Darya or Oxus River, nicknamed the "Mad River" due to its tendency to change course or overflood erratically.

Over the years, the citadel has managed to withstand assault after assault by the waters of the Oxus, but its defenses have gradually worn out. Though the main structure of the fortress is still standing, it is partly ruined, and local authorities have deemed it no longer safe to use on a large scale, and the administration has relocated to other structures in town.

Still, at least the citadel remains standing. Even if it is no longer in frequent use, it will surely continue to inspire and embolden the inhabitants nearby."

before: RICE_granada_alhambra_decision_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historischer Kontext:#! Die Alhambra (von arabisch #italic Al-Hamra#!, was "die Rote" bedeutet) war ein Palast- und Festungskomplex der Nasriden-Dynastie von Granada und der Inbegriff der mittelalterlichen maurischen Architektur. before:
granada.0014.desc:0 "Ich habe in meinem Herrenhaus in [granada.GetNameNoTier] geschlafen, als mich meine Wachen spät in der Nacht geweckt haben - auf den Straßen der Stadt ist das Chaos ausgebrochen!

Anscheinend hatte sich heute früh ein falsches Gerücht verbreitet, dass der jüdische Beamte [yusuf.GetFullName] und andere Juden zu einem feindlichen Herrscher übergelaufen seien, die Stadttore geöffnet und mich ermordet hätten. Aufgrund der in letzter Zeit zunehmenden judenfeindlichen Stimmung hat sich schnell ein Mob gebildet, um die Stadt zu "schützen". Offensichtlich bin ich am Leben und [granada.GetNameNoTierNoTooltip] ist in Sicherheit.

Ehe ich mich versehe, kommt [yusuf.GetFirstName] in Panik an und bittet um Hilfe. Wenige Augenblicke später stürmt der Mob meinen Palast und schreit, dass sie den "Verräter" [yusuf.GetFirstName] töten werden, bevor sie sich als nächstes seine jüdischen Mitbürger vornehmen. Ich eile zu der versammelten Menge, um ihnen zu versichern, dass es mir gut geht, und fordere sie auf, sich zurückzuziehen, aber sie schenken mir keine Beachtung.

Die Menge bewegt sich nun schnell auf [yusuf.GetFirstName] zu, und ich und meine Wachen haben kaum Zeit zu reagieren."

before: granada.0082.desc:0 "Ein Reisender aus der Ferne stattet mir heute einen Besuch ab. Dieser Mann kann nicht anders, als die Schönheit der Landschaft von [ROOT.Char.GetCapitalLocation.GetCounty.GetTitle.GetNameNoTier] zu loben.\n\n"Ich war skeptisch, bevor ich hierher kam", gibt er zu, "aber wenn ich all die Täler, die Trockengebiete, die Wälder, die Berge und die Flüsse sehe.... Es fällt mir schwer, die Herrlichkeit dieses Ortes zu beschreiben. Es ist wie eine perfekte Mischung aus verschiedenen Klimazonen, der perfekte Mittelweg zwischen den Extremen. Ihr seid gesegnet, hier zu leben, [ROOT.Char.GetTitledFirstName], und ich bin sicher, Euer Land ist friedlich und wohlhabend. Wenn ich könnte, würde ich mich hier niederlassen, aber das ist nicht mein Schicksal, wie es scheint, denn ich habe meine Pflichten.""

before: RICE_manichean_mani_sealstone_desc:0 "Long ago, the Prophet Mani, founder of the [manichean_faith.GetAdjective] Church, was said to possess a crystal stone seal that depicted himself flanked by two followers. Generations of faithful [manichean_faith.GetAdherentNamePluralNoTooltip] kept it as a relic after his passion and [Glossary( 'parinirvana', 'MANICHEAN_PARINIRVANA_GLOSS' )]. before: activity_RICE_manichean_bema_festival_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historical Context:#! before: RICE_tro_breizh_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historischer Kontextt:#! Obwohl lokale Pilgerfahrten seit Jahrhunderten ein wichtiger Bestandteil der bretonischen Kultur sind (wie in vielen anderen Teilen der christlichen Welt), ist "Tro Breizh" ein moderner Begriff und ein Konzept, das hier der Einfachheit halber verwendet wird, um historische Pilgerfahrten in der Region zu beschreiben. Die Wallfahrt fand jährlich statt, dauerte einen Monat und führte zu den Kathedralen der sieben ältesten Bischofsstädte der Bretagne. Diese Orte wurden der Reihe nach besucht. Mithin wurden in rund 30 Tagen über 550 km zurückgelegt. Es war unter strenggläubigen Katholiken Brauch, mindestens einmal im Leben am Tro-Breizh teilzunehmen. Die Gläubigen erhoffen durch die Teilnahme an der Wallfahrt eine Vergebung ihrer Sünden zu erlangen. Die Tro-Breizh hatte daher für die Katholiken eine so große Bedeutung, dass die Wallfahrt notfalls auch nach dem Tod im Sarg zurückgelegt wurde."

before: breton.0028.desc:0 "Ich bin fast fertig mit der Tro Breizh, denn ich komme jetzt in Vannes an, der siebten und letzten Etappe dieser Pilgerreise. Obwohl es sich um eine sehr alte Ortschaft handelt - sie geht auf die Zeit vor den römischen Kaisern zurück, wie mir Gelehrte sagten - ist es auch ein sehr fröhlicher und lebhafter Ort. Ich habe mich zum Beispiel sehr über die komisch aufgeblasenen, potthässlichen Granitstatuen amüsiert, die die Einheimischen als "Vannes und sein Weib" bezeichnen. Einige der Einheimischen erläuterten mir auch die Geschichte der großen Steine, die in der Gegend verstreut sind.\n\nAber dies ist eine Zeit der Frömmigkeit, nicht der Heiterkeit. Ich denke an den Schutzpatron von Vannes, den Heiligen Patern. Man sagt, dieser Heilige sei ein Zeitgenosse des mächtigen Königs Artus, des großen britischen Helden, gewesen; er habe den Geiz des Königs gebändigt und den Monarchen gedemütigt, heißt es in den Legenden. Auch ich jedenfalls muss mich in den Tugenden üben. Deshalb habe ich mich ja auf diese Pilgerreise begeben."

before: breton.0054.desc:0 "In der Bretagne gibt es eine seltene, unscheinbare Pflanze, die als Goldgras oder "aour iaotenn" bekannt ist. Es ist schwer zu finden und kann nur von einem tugendhaften Menschen entdeckt werden, so die Legende. Jedenfalls hat eine für ihre Tugendhaftigkeit bekannte bretonische Bauersfrau wohl etwas von diesem goldenen Gras gefunden und bietet es mir an. Wenn man es als Trank zu sich nimmt, kann man angeblich seine Manneskraft verzehnfachen."

before: breton.0061.desc:0 "Ich bin in einer örtlichen Taverne, ruhe mich aus und genieße gutes Essen und Trinken. Heute Abend ist ein Barde anwesend, der verschiedene bretonische Märchen zum Besten gibt. Eine davon handelt von einem Wesen, das als Bugul Noz (der "Nachtschäfer") bekannt ist und in den Wäldern der Bretagne wohnt. Obwohl er abscheulich aussieht - so abscheulich, dass manche vor Angst krepieren, wenn sie ihn sehen - ist er in Wirklichkeit eine sehr sanfte und freundliche Seele, der Inbegriff der Güte. Wenn jemand in der Nähe ist, ruft er ihm zu, er solle weggehen, damit er sich nicht erschreckt und sicher nach Hause gehen kann. Auf diese Weise hilft er den Menschen, gefährliche Gegenden in der Nacht zu meiden."

before: RICE_magadha_inspired_bodhi_tree_navel_of_the_earth_desc:0 "Nachdem er den Bodhi-Baum in Gaya besucht hatte, wurde dieser Charakter von den buddhistischen Legenden inspiriert, die besagen, warum dieser Ort als "Nabel der Erde" gilt. Es heißt, dass dieser Ort als einziger in der Lage ist, das Gewicht der Erleuchtung des Buddha zu tragen, und es heißt auch, dass der Bodhi-Baum der letzte Ort sein wird, der verschwindet, wenn diese Welt am Ende dieses Kalpa zerstört wird, und dass er auch der erste sein wird, der wieder erscheint, wenn ein neues Kalpa beginnt."

before: RICE_magadha_claim_pithipati_title_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historischer Kontext:#! #italic Pithipati#! war ein Titel, der von der lokalen Chikore-Dynastie im mittelalterlichen Indien verwendet wurde und Herr des Diamantenthrons bedeutet. before:
bao.0001.desc:0 "Meine Soldaten bringen zwei junge Männer in schwarzer Kleidung, die sie vor meinem Haus festgenommen haben.

"Dieses niedere Gesindel wurde schlafend in einem ausgetrockneten Graben gefunden, mein [ROOT.Char.GetLadyLord]", sagt einer meiner Soldaten auf die Frage, wer sie seien. Ein anderer Soldat wirft ein: "Ich stimme zwar zu, dass sie sich verdächtig verhalten, aber wir sollten nicht zu voreilig urteilen.

before: bao.0001.info:0 "#emphasis Historischer Kontext:#! Bis zur Mitte des 20. Jahrhunderts waren Trachten das zuverlässigste Mittel, um den sozialen Status eines Fremden zu erkennen; in der Bretagne waren schwarze Trachten die unverhüllten Gewänder für die Ärmsten der Armen. Die "Sonerien Du" oder "Schwarzen Musikanten" waren reisende Sänger und Musiker, die hauptsächlich mit Speis und Trank bezahlt wurden und von Kirche zu Kirche, von Messe zu Messe und von Hochzeit zu Hochzeit zogen, um ihren Beruf auszuüben. Sie hatten den Ruf, "hep diskrog" oder "rastlos" zu spielen, und dem örtlichen Aberglauben zufolge konnte eine bretonische Hochzeit nur dann zu Ende gehen, wenn der Musikant zu betrunken zum Spielen war. Sie wurden von den Gendarmen und den oberen Schichten der bretonischen Gesellschaft oft als Unruhestifter angesehen.\n Die eigentliche "Sonerien Du"-Legende, auf die sich das Ereignis bezieht, ist die Legende der Bro Vigouden (Baronie Kemper), in der zwei schwarzgekleidete Musiker um 1790 in Pont-'n-Abad (Pont-l'-Abbé auf Französisch) zu Unrecht bestraft und zum Tode verurteilt wurden, weil sie betrunken am Straßenrand schliefen, entweder weil sie fälschlicherweise für Straßenräuber gehalten wurden oder als Folge der Korruption der örtlichen Aristokratie. Ihre Leichen wurden für alle sichtbar auf Spießen ausgesetzt. Da dieses Ereignis mit (nicht bestätigten) Pestausbrüchen zusammenfiel, hielt man sie für Märtyrer und berührte die Leichen, weil man glaubte, dass dies Immunität gegen die Pest gewähren würde."

before: guanche.0012.desc:0 Nach drei Tagen des Fastens fahren ich und viele andere mit unserem Vieh zu einem der höchsten Gipfel von [rain_ritual_county.GetName], um dort in einem Gehege ein Heiligtum zu errichten. before: guanche.0052.desc:0 Wir hätten handeln müssen, aber jetzt ist es zu spät. Die rapide schwindenden Holzbestände auf [madeira_county.GetNameNoTier] waren die Warnzeichen, die wir missachtet haben. Es ist schwer vorstellbar, dass Madeira, die Insel des unendlichen Holzes, eines Tages nicht mehr genug Holz haben würde, um ihre Zuckerindustrie aufrechtzuerhalten, aber dieser Tag ist gekommen. Händler, die Madeiras einst weitläufige Zuckerrohrfarmen und fleißige Zuckermühlen besitzen und betreiben, haben mir erzählt, dass die Zuckerproduktion aufgrund des plötzlichen Mangels an lokal verfügbarem Holz auf einem historischen Tiefstand ist und die Zuckerindustrie der Insel schnell zusammenbricht. Auch wenn sich die Zuckerindustrie hier eines Tages wieder erholen könnte, wird sie auf importiertes Holz angewiesen sein und nie wieder ihre einstigen glorreichen Höhen erreichen."

before:
game_concept_mahavihara_desc:0 "The Mahavihara, alongside the [abhayagiri|E] and [jetavana|E], are one of the three major [RICE_sri_lanka_monasteries|E] in the [RICE_sri_lanka_struggle|E], or its Buddhist community. In-game, the Mahavihara are represented by an orange icon: @RICE_mahavihara_icon!.

You can raise or lower the [RICE_sri_lanka_prominence|E] of the Mahavihara through different [decisions|E], [activities|E], and so on, especially if you have the [GetTrait('RICE_mahavihara_trait').GetName( GetNullCharacter )] [trait|E], which can be gained by taking the [decision|E] to $RICE_sri_lanka_choose_monastic_sect$. Keep this in mind if you wish to end the [struggle|E] in [RICE_sri_lanka_short|E].

Historically, the Mahavihara were the more 'traditionalist' monastery or sect of ancient and medieval Sri Lankan Buddhism. They were typically skeptical or dismissive of what they saw as heterodox ideas from India. According to traditional chronicles, they were the ones who "won" out in the end against the other monasteries."

before: RICE_sri_lanka_worship_local_deities_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historical Context:#! For centuries, the people of Sri Lanka have worshipped a variety of shared deities, regardless of whether they are Buddhist or Hindu, or Sinhala, Tamil, or Vedda. Many of these deities were syncretized forms of Hindu, Buddhist, and indigenous religious figures, known by different names from different communities and often worshipped in a manner distinct from mainland India. Some were even historical Sri Lankan figures like kings turned into deities. For the island's Buddhists, while the Buddha is considered superior to these "lesser" deities, the latter are often invoked for more worldly concerns."

before:
sri_lanka.0103.desc.dharmadhatu:0 "The chanting of prayers ring in the air, and the march of people and elephants, as the procession and worship ceremony begins.

We pray to remind ourselves about the importance of the Three Jewels – the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha – as we make offerings where the Dharmadhatu lays. I reflect on the Dharmadhatu while doing so.

The text itself expounds on the #italic Trikaya#! or "three bodies" teaching on the nature of reality and Buddhahood, found in the [GetDoctrineType('rice_mahayana_canon_doctrine').GetBaseName]. Some detractors criticize the Dharmadhatu’s teachings as unorthodox, even heretical, but others believe its spiritual ideas can help and guide all, and so it is worthy of veneration."

before:
socotra.0009.desc:0 "We have tolerated the presence of pirates in my territories for far too long. Our "agreements" with them have not been working in our favor, and even though many are also respectable merchants, can we really trust them when they are no less greedier than the average charlatan and bandit?

I have thus sent out an order to immediately renege on any of our agreements with pirate groups in the [GetGeographicalRegion('RICE_indian_ocean_region').GetName]. They will no longer be afforded legal protections nor the ability to set up their base of operations in my territories by working with us, because they no longer work #italic for#! us.

I have ordered my troops to make sure these pirates comply with our commands. We can only hope they leave peaceably...."

before: RICE_bamian_repair_shahr_e_zohak_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historical Context:#! Shahr-e Zohak is one of the most impressive fortifications ever built in Afghanistan; one scholar even called it the "Afghan Krak des Chevaliers." It was occupied by successive groups, such as the Hephthalites, Ghaznavids, Ghurids, and Timurids. Zohak is an evil figure in Persian mythology, and though it is uncertain why the fortress is named after him, he is said to be the ancestor of the nearby Ghurids. A legend has it that the fortress city was destroyed by Genghis Khan, and all its inhabitants massacred as revenge for his grandson's death when it was besieged."

before: RICE_galicia_pray_to_santiago_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historical Context:#! before:
normandy.0091.info:0 "
#emphasis Historical Context:#! Whatever the truth of William and Matilda's relationship, there are legends of questionable veracity about how it began. Supposedly, Matilda rejected William's offer of marriage, as she saw herself, daughter of the Count Baldwin of Flanders, as too high-born for a "bastard."

The Duke, in his rage, went all the way to her home in Flanders. In some versions of the legend, he found her going to church and, in broad daylight, dragged her off her horse by her braids and pushed her into the mud before riding off. In other variations, he went to her father's manor, and dragged her by her braids or hit her in full view of everyone, Baldwin included. Afterwards, Matilda bizarrely only wanted to marry William.

In reality, the marriage was probably arranged under more mundane political circumstances. The Counts of Flanders were powerful, and a potential threat to Normandy's east. By marrying into their family, William not only avoided conflict with them, but also gained a valuable ally."

before: aachen.0024.desc.lothair:0 "\n\nThe #V Lotharkreuz#! wird häufig bei heiligen Prozessionen in Aachen verwendet. Ihren Namen verdankt sie dem eingravierten, grünen Kristallsiegel in der Nähe ihres Sockels, das den Namen eines Urenkels Karls des Großen, König Lothar II, trägt. Der Eichenkern ist mit Gold und Silber ummantelt und mit zahlreichen Edelsteinen verziert. Dort, wo sich die Arme des Kreuzes treffen, befindet sich eine Onyxschnitzerei von Augustus Caesar, die auf die Römerzeit zurückgeht. Darunter befindet sich ein Siegel mit der Inschrift: "Christus, hilf König Lothar!"

before: RICE_khuzestan_khuzi_status_decision_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historical Context:#! Early medieval Islamic sources mention the existence of a so-called Khuzi people, who spoke a language that modern scholars theorize to be a late remnant of ancient Elamite. Although Khuzi was spoken by local nobility, this may have been because they learned it from their servants (such as wet-nurses, bathroom attendants, and so on). The Khuzis were otherwise treated as low status; for example, #italic "yā Xuz̄ı!"#!, meaning "Hey, you Khuzi!" was reported by the 10th century Arab geographer Al-Maqdisi as a common, slang term of insult in the region. Because of this, the Khuzi identity and language likely faded away as the Khuzis assimilated into Arab or Iranian populations."

before:
north_atlantic.0208.info:0 "
#emphasis Historical Context:#! Dairy products have been consumed in Northern and Western Europe for centuries, and #italic skyr#! is the name of the Icelandic variant of yogurt. Interestingly, in the Icelandic sagas, serving items like milk, cheese, or yogurt to guests was considered improper, particularly if other food could be provided. Being immersed in milk products could be considered especially humiliating.

In one episode of the #italic Egil's Saga#!, for instance, the protagonist Egil and his companions visit a man named Armod, who only serves them #italic skyr#!. Egil takes this as a great insult, and, in revenge, vomits the yogurt all over Armod, who in turn vomits back at Egil. When Armod's men ask why Egil did such a thing, he says, "Don’t blame me for following the master of the house’s example. He’s spewing his guts out just as much as I am.""

north_atlantic.0273.desc:0 "Though I am young, I have already learned much from the schools here in the British Isles. The skies are marked with numberless sparks, each a fire, and I know these stars well. I have seen in these stars that it is perhaps my time to travel far from here, and learn more and more about this world. Maybe, one day, I can even become one of the greatest astrologers in the world.

before: RICE_pamir_restore_hephthalite_empire_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historical Context:#! The Hephthalites, sometimes called the White Huns, were a major wave of "Hunnic" tribal invaders into Persia and India in the 4th and 5th centuries. Their relationship with "Hunnic" groups like the Kidarites and Xionites, the ethnic differences between these groups (if any), and where they came from, is still debated in academic circles - there are too many theories to be listed here, but suffice to say, Iranian and Turkic influence in their origins is likely, and it is possible that the Pamirs are their homeland. A Persian and Turkic alliance defeated them in c. 560 CE and the Hephthalite Empire split into many petty chiefdoms. Prominent among these Hephthalite rump states were the Turkshahis and their cousins, the Zunbils."

before:
normandy.0091.info:0 "
#emphasis Historical Context:#! Whatever the truth of William and Matilda's relationship, there are legends of questionable veracity about how it began. Supposedly, Matilda rejected William's offer of marriage, as she saw herself, daughter of the Count Baldwin of Flanders, as too high-born for a "bastard."

The Duke, in his rage, went all the way to her home in Flanders. In some versions of the legend, he found her going to church and, in broad daylight, dragged her off her horse by her braids and pushed her into the mud before riding off. In other variations, he went to her father's manor, and dragged her by her braids or hit her in full view of everyone, Baldwin included. Afterwards, Matilda bizarrely only wanted to marry William.

In reality, the marriage was probably arranged under more mundane political circumstances. The Counts of Flanders were powerful, and a potential threat to Normandy's east. By marrying into their family, William not only avoided conflict with them, but also gained a valuable ally."

before:
harran.0062.desc:0 "I sit in the darkness of my library, sipping mint tea as my acquaintance enters the room. He is a scholar from the House of Wisdom who I worked with back when I lived in Baghdad, and he gives a smile as he joins me. I offer him some tea, and we chat pleasantly about various topics to catch up.

Eventually, our conversation drifts towards the topic of religion. "I heard something interesting about your grandfather [hilal_al_sabi.GetFullName] the other day," my friend tells me.

This again? I shift uncomfortably, but don't say anything yet, and continue sipping my tea."

He is a scholar from the House of Wisdom who I worked with back when I lived in Baghdad, and he gives a smile as he joins me. I offer him some tea, and we chat pleasantly about various topics to catch up.

Eventually, our conversation drifts towards the topic of religion. "I heard something interesting about your grandfather [hilal_al_sabi.GetFullName] the other day," my friend tells me.

This again? I shift uncomfortably, but don't say anything yet, and continue sipping my tea."

before:
harran.0063.desc:0 "“You have said for many years that your grandfather converted to Islam thanks to a dream, a sure sign from Allah himself.” My friend smiles. "One of my mentors, an older gentleman, who was acquainted with your grandfather, said he never heard of such a thing, but admits perhaps his memory is not as it used to be thanks to old age. I don’t doubt you, but it does make me wonder if your grandfather was telling the truth - no offense to him.” 

I stroke my chin and gaze at my friend quietly. Many question my grandfather's story. I know this.

I ponder how to respond."

before: harran.0064.desc:0 ""Perhaps my mentor misremembered due to old age," my acquaintance shrugs. "I don't mean to question your own faith, of course. I just thought it was something interesting. No matter, I am probably  making you uncomfortable, so I apologize."\n\n"Of course," I say politely. We sip tea for a few more moments, savoring the taste, before I continue: "Now, not to change the subject, but have you read the new treatise written by….""

before:
harran.0065.desc:0 "“But what?” he says.

I frown.

"I don't mean to imply he was secretly an apostate, but…." I consider my words carefully. "I always felt he had sympathy for his birth religion. I could tell by the way he talked fondly of our ancestors."

"The scholarly achievements of Harran's pagans are nothing to laugh at! Your forebear, [thabit_ibn_qurra.GetFullName], was a rare scholar of his age." My friend nods. "But if your grandfather's heart is genuine, thanks to that dream, then that is all that matters. Sure, you still have a few wayward relatives who still believe your old gods, and I know you were never the most pious man, but at least you are a believer, too, right?""

before: RICE_granada_alhambra_decision_context_tooltip:0 "#emphasis Historical Context:#! The Alhambra (from Arabic #italic Al-Hamra#!, meaning "the Red One") was a palace and fortress complex of the Nasrid dynasty of Granada, and the epitome of medieval Moorish architecture. before:
granada.0014.desc:0 "I was sleeping at my manor in [granada.GetNameNoTier] when my guards woke me late at night - chaos has erupted in the city's streets!

Apparently, a false rumor had spread earlier today that the Jewish official [yusuf.GetFullName] and other Jews had defected to an enemy ruler, opened the city gates, and killed me. Thanks to recent, rising anti-Jewish sentiment, a mob quickly formed to "protect" the city. Obviously, I’m alive and [granada.GetNameNoTierNoTooltip] is safe.

Before I know it, [yusuf.GetFirstName] arrives in a panic, begging for help. Moments later, the mob storms my palace, screaming how they will kill the "traitor" [yusuf.GetFirstName] before going for his fellow Jews next. I rush to meet the mob to reassure them that I am fine and demand they stand down, but they pay no heed.

The mob is now moving fast towards [yusuf.GetFirstName], and I and my guards have little time to react."

before:
VIETkemet.0003.desc:0 "After changing into humbler clothes, my companions and I now look like ordinary if well-off travelers. The villagers are hospitable to us "travelers" and happily provide us accommodations. It is auspicious that we have come at this time, they say.

Standing in the village square, in the midst of a throng of men, women, and children, I watch as the feast to Osiris proceeds. Some villagers take pigs with them and bring the animals before an altar of the god. They slit the throats of the unfortunate beasts, an offering no doubt to Osiris, before giving the carcasses to swineherds who take the bodies away.

Afterwards, a great cheer erupts, as everyone begins to fill the village square to celebrate. I enjoy drinking good beer and dancing with the other villagers. Soon enough, one villager, playing the flutes, happily skips around playing a lively tune, and we all follow after him while singing praises to Osiris."

before:
